brief_summary: Five numbered panels mapping reader workflow profiles to a recommended keyboard size: programmer without a heavy layer habit to 75% or TKL, gamer to 65% or TKL, spreadsheet-heavy work to full-size or TKL plus numpad, minimalist/travel buyer to 65% or 60%, and a reader already fluent with layers (e.g. Vim) to 60%. Recommendations are drawn directly from the article's 'Matching the size to the actual workflow' section.
data_sources: keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'Matching the size to the actual workflow' — 'That combination makes 75% or TKL the more defensible default' (programmers)
keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'Matching the size to the actual workflow' — '65% or TKL both serve that well' (gamers)

keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'Matching the size to the actual workflow' — 'Readers who genuinely touch-type numbers all day are shopping for full-size or a TKL-plus-separate-numpad combo' (spreadsheet-heavy work)
keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'Matching the size to the actual workflow' — 'Minimalists and travel-focused buyers are the group 60% and 65% were built for'

keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a firmware layer buys back' — 'A programmer who's already fluent in a heavily-layered editor (Vim-style modal navigation, for instance) is the exception that makes 65% or even 60% work well'
